hints: Find tangent to $C_1$ at $x = 3$: $\frac{dy}{dx} = 2(3) - 4 = 2$ at $(3, 4) \implies y = 2x - 2$.
Set discriminant $\Delta = (-12)^2 - 16(4 - k) = 0$ to find $k = -5$, and solve for $P\left(\frac{3}{2}, 1\right)$.
walkthrough:
Find the equation of the tangent line to $C_1$ ($y = x^2 - 4x + 7$) at $x = 3$:
$$y_1(3) = 3^2 - 4(3) + 7 = 9 - 12 + 7 = 4$$
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x - 4 \implies \left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{x=3} = 2(3) - 4 = 2$$
$$y - 4 = 2(x - 3) \implies y = 2x - 2$$

Substitute the tangent line equation into curve $C_2$ ($y^2 = 4x + k$):
$$(2x - 2)^2 = 4x + k \implies 4x^2 - 8x + 4 = 4x + k \implies 4x^2 - 12x + (4 - k) = 0$$

Apply the tangency condition requiring discriminant $\Delta = 0$:
$$(-12)^2 - 4(4)(4 - k) = 0 \implies 144 - 16(4 - k) = 0$$
$$16(4 - k) = 144 \implies 4 - k = 9 \implies k = -5$$

Substitute $k = -5$ back into the quadratic to find point $P$:
$$4x^2 - 12x + 9 = 0 \implies (2x - 3)^2 = 0 \implies x = \frac{3}{2}$$
$$y = 2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 2 = 3 - 2 = 1$$
$$k = -5, \quad P = \left(\frac{3}{2}, 1\right)$$
